title: Lesson 1: What is Force
explanation: Force is not a thing you see directly. It is inferred from change in motion. Imagine a bowling ball at rest. When a hand pushes it and it moves, that invisible interaction is force: a push or pull that changes motion.

questions.explanation: Force is an interaction described as a push or pull.

questions.prompt: What indicates a force is acting?
questions.explanation: We infer force when motion changes.

questions.prompt: You can see force directly, like seeing color on an object.
questions.explanation: Force is inferred from interaction outcomes, not observed directly.

questions.prompt: Which is the best real-world example of force?
options: A book sitting on a table

questions.prompt: A push on a bowling ball can change how fast it moves.
questions.explanation: Force changes motion — speed or direction.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg object accelerates at 2 m/s². Find the force (F = ma).

options: Something that exists even if nothing changes
questions.explanation: Force is inferred from interaction outcomes, not seen directly.

questions.prompt: A 10 N force acts on a 5 kg mass. What is acceleration (m/s²)?
If net force on an object is zero, its velocity must be zero.
questions.explanation: Zero net force means constant velocity — which can be zero or non-zero.

curiosityNodes.prompt: Why can't we see force directly?
curiosityNodes.expansion: Force is invisible because it is a model for interaction. We only observe its signature: acceleration, deformation, or change in motion — like the bowling ball starting to roll.

curiosityNodes.prompt: What if nothing pushes the bowling ball?
curiosityNodes.expansion: Without a net external interaction, the ball keeps its current state. No push means no change from rest; no opposing force means motion does not stop by itself in an ideal case.

curiosityNodes.prompt: How does a harder push change the scene?
curiosityNodes.expansion: A stronger push increases acceleration — motion lines lengthen, force arrows intensify, but the bowling ball anchor stays the same object in the chamber.

reinforcementFeedback.correct: Great read. You recognized force as an interaction causing motion change.
reinforcementFeedback.incorrect: Re-focus on the core model: force is inferred from changes in motion, not observed directly.
